answer: Approximately 50 million to 100 million people died in the 1918 influenza pandemic worldwide, with 50 million being a commonly cited baseline estimate. In the United States, approximately 675,000 people died. Death toll estimates have evolved significantly over time; earlier estimates from the 1920s suggested around 21.6 million deaths, but modern reassessments based on more comprehensive data indicate substantially higher figures of 50-100 million globally, reflecting better accounting of deaths across different regions.
sources: Web search - 50-100M global deaths, ~675,000 US, citing Cleveland Clinic, Stanford and others
